description: ol-reserved-word (issue #739): the two boundaries of the binding-position rule, pinned together. (1) A binding introduces a `:name` VARIABLE, and spec/grammar.md:369 keeps variables out of the one callable namespace primitives, user procedures, and struct constructors share — so `:count = 3` (the Core primitive `count`) and `:helper = 4` (a procedure defined in this same program) stay clean. Only the reserved-word category collides from a binding position; the registration forms keep their full four-category check, which reserved-word-local-primitive covers. (2) Only a BARE place head introduces a name: `:repeat = [1 2]` is flagged once at line 7, while the nested write `:repeat[1] = 5` on line 8 stores into the structure that binding already created and is not flagged again — spec/grammar.md:369, "selector bare keys are data, not declarations". The single expected diagnostic is therefore the whole point: seven statements, exactly one finding. `"check": true` (semantic-checker only) — nothing is executed and no events are produced.
